title: Hand Washing & Food Safety — Required Test
description: Finishing this test is required to keep working at Ayvaz Pizza. Answer each question, then check it. You will see straight away whether you got it right and why.

questions.title: Hand washing is the MOST effective way to prevent the spread of what?
questions.explanation: Washing your hands is the single best thing you do all shift. It stops the germs that make customers sick, and it stops the ones that go around the team.

questions.title: How long must hands be lathered with soap during proper hand washing?
questions.explanation: At least 20 seconds of scrubbing, every time. "Until they feel clean" is not a measure — hands feel clean long before they are.

questions.title: Singing the "Happy Birthday" song twice equals the required hand-washing time.
questions.explanation: Twice through is about 20 seconds. It is a way to count without a clock on the wall.

questions.title: Which sink is the ONLY approved place to wash your hands?
questions.explanation: The hand sink, and nothing else. The prep sink is for food, the 3-compartment sink is for dishes, and the mop sink is the dirtiest thing in the building.

questions.title: Washing your hands at a prep sink is acceptable if the hand sink is busy.
questions.explanation: Never. Washing your hands in the prep sink puts what was on your hands where the food goes. Wait for the hand sink.

questions.title: You are allowed to wash your hands while wearing disposable gloves.
questions.explanation: Gloves do not get washed. They come off and go in the bin, then you wash your hands, then you put a new pair on.

questions.title: How many times are you required to wash and sanitize your hands to complete and box an order by yourself that has both wings and pizza?
questions.explanation: Four. Every time you move between raw and ready-to-eat, or change gloves, that is another wash — doing the whole order yourself means doing it four times.

questions.title: Watch this short video. Which steps did Pepper MISS? Click all that apply.
questions.help: Watch it twice before you answer. Check it against the order you know, step by step.
choices: She did not lather for a full 20 seconds
She did not turn off the tap with a paper towel
She did not apply hand sanitizer
She did not wet her hands before the soap
She did not use soap at all
She did not rinse the soap off
She did not dry her hands
questions.explanation: Three things. She rushed the lather — it has to be a full 20 seconds, every time. She turned the tap off with her bare hand, which puts straight back what she just washed off; that is what the paper towel is for. And she never applied sanitizer, which goes on after drying. The washing she did do was fine — wet, soap, rinse, dry.

questions.title: After using the restroom, when must you wash your hands?
choices: Only if you touched the door
Before leaving the restroom AND again at the BOH hand sink
questions.explanation: Twice. Once in the restroom before you leave, then again at the back-of-house hand sink — because you touched the restroom door on the way out.

questions.title: Touching your apron, hat, shirt, face, hair, glasses, or cell phone requires hand washing before returning to work.
questions.explanation: All of them. Your phone is the one people forget, and it is the dirtiest thing you touch all day.

questions.title: When must a delivery driver wash and sanitize their hands after returning from a delivery?
choices: Only if their hands look dirty
Immediately upon returning, before handling or cutting food
Only at the end of their shift
questions.explanation: The moment they are back, before they touch any food. They have handled car doors, money and somebody's front door since they last washed.

questions.title: Hand sanitizer can replace hand washing if hands look clean.
questions.explanation: Sanitizer never replaces washing. It goes on after washing and drying, not instead of it, and hands that look clean are not clean.

questions.title: When should hand sanitizer be applied?
questions.explanation: Last. Wash, dry, then sanitize. On wet hands it is watered down and does nothing.

questions.title: What should you use to turn off the faucet after washing your hands?
questions.explanation: A paper towel. You turned that faucet on with dirty hands, so turning it off with clean ones puts everything straight back.

questions.title: When must hands be washed related to gloves?
choices: Before putting on gloves AND every time gloves are changed
questions.explanation: Before the gloves go on, and again every single time you change them. A clean glove over a dirty hand is still a dirty hand.

questions.title: Put these in the correct order for proper hand washing.
steps: Lather Hands and Wrists (at least 20 seconds)
Turn Off Faucets (with Paper Towel If not Hands Free)
questions.explanation: Wet, soap, lather for 20 seconds, rinse, dry, turn off the faucet with the towel, then sanitizer. The two people get wrong: turning off the faucet with clean bare hands, and putting sanitizer on before drying.
